transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I came in because I just can't seem to stop worrying. It's like I'm worrying about everything all at once. I'm constantly stressing over my marriage, whether my performance is slipping at work, the bills... even the house projects I keep starting and dropping. I just have this constant worry that I'm basically failing as a husband and a father, and I really don't know how to turn it off anymore.
How long have you been experiencing this constant worrying—has it been going on for six months or more, or did it start more recently after a particular event?

It's definitely been more than six months. I'd say it's been going on for about nine months now. It really started getting this bad when a big cloud migration project ramped up at work, and right around that same time, the arguments at home started becoming a regular thing.
Along with the worrying, have you noticed physical symptoms like feeling restless or on edge, muscle tension, or getting tired easily?

Yeah, definitely. I feel... well, wound tight almost all day. It's like my shoulders are completely locked up and I'm just constantly bracing for something. And I definitely get restless, too. I catch myself pacing back and forth between my meetings, or even when I'm at chess club, I'm constantly tapping the pieces. Sitting still just feels impossible right now.
Do you also find yourself worrying excessively about things that have nothing to do with the work project or the arguments at home—like your health, world events, or other everyday matters?

No, not really. I don't think I focus much on world events or my health, to be honest. It's pretty much just... well, the things in my own life that I mentioned before. The job, my marriage, the house projects, the bills. I mean, that stuff is already taking up all my mental space, so I haven't really noticed myself stressing over the news or getting sick or anything outside of that.
When things are going relatively okay at work or home for a day or two, does the worry still stay just as intense, or does it noticeably ease up during those calmer periods?

It doesn't really ease up, honestly. Even on a quiet day, when I tell myself to just... focus on the code right in front of me, or try to breathe through a workout, my brain just won't let it go. It's like one concern just hooks onto another. Before I know it, I'm twenty steps ahead, imagining some minor issue turning into a bad performance review, which leads to me losing my job, and then my family being worse off because of me. So, yeah, it just spirals, even when things are supposedly calm.

latest_inference.note: The worry persists at full intensity even during calm periods when stressors ease, arguing against an adjustment disorder (F43.22) where anxiety would be expected to fluctuate with the stressor. Combined with >6 months duration, multiple worry domains, and physical symptoms (muscle tension, restlessness), this is most consistent with GAD.
